messages.subject: Re: MSstats::dataProcess RAM overflow for SpectroNaut input
messages.subject_clean: MSstats::dataProcess RAM overflow for SpectroNaut input
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Since we've recently run into a similar problem again, I'd like to share here our current workaround to overcome the issue with non-converging imputation, until the announced MSstats workflow for large SpectroNaut files will be released:

Setting the dataProcess parameter "featureSubset" to "topN" with "n_top_feature" = 1000 did the trick.
(In our current sample there was only a single protein (titin) in our (muscle) sample with > 1000 peptides per protein (4522), which likely also was the reason for the stalled imputation.)

Best,
Christian

Christian Schori schrieb am Mittwoch, 23. März 2022 um 10:32:10 UTC+1:
> Hi Mateusz,
>
> Thank you for this tip. MBimpute = FALSE did the trick. - But I still don't really understand, why this is happening? How can the imputation process chew up all the RAM? Based on the number of censoredInt, only about 8% of all intensities need imputation. Is there something wrong with our input file, or is there a bug in the imputation process?
>
> In addition, I've also checked with the suggested MSstatsSummarize method:
>
> raw = SN_to_MSstatsformat_import
> method = "TMP"
> cens = "NA"
> impute = TRUE
> MSstatsConvert::MSstatsLogsSettings(FALSE)
> input = MSstatsPrepareForDataProcess(raw, 2, NULL)
> input = MSstatsNormalize(input, "EQUALIZEMEDIANS")
> input = MSstatsMergeFractions(input)
> input = MSstatsHandleMissing(input, "TMP", TRUE, "NA", 0.999)
> input = MSstatsSelectFeatures(input, "all")
> processed = getProcessed(input)
> input = MSstatsPrepareForSummarization(input, method, impute, cens, FALSE)
> input_split = split(input, input$PROTEIN)
> summarized = MSstatsSummarize(input_split, method, impute, cens, FALSE, TRUE)
> output = MSstatsSummarizationOutput(input, summarized, processed, method, impute, cens)
>
> Again, the process produced a memory overflow at the "MSstatsSummarize" step, resulting R to crash. Using the same approach with "impute = FALSE" did run through...
>
> Best regards,
> Christian
>

I've just tried to reprocess this file with the suggested settings for R (R_MAX_VSIZE=300Gb) on our Ubunutu-Desktop with 188Gb RAM and monitored the RAM (with htop). As before, dataProcess runs nicely for about 5 to 10minutes, with an average 6-8Gb of RAM usage, and then skyrockets using the complete 188Gb of RAM resulting in R to crash. Interestingly the progress bar for this step is stuck at 0% for the whole time. Would there be a way to monitor the vector memory usage during this process? - Although I'm not so sure if this is really the root cause of this issue... In general, I don't really understand, why we don't have this issue for other (even bigger) Spectronaut datasets...
> > >
> > > Could this behavior even be sample-type dependent? (I know this sounds far-fetched and a bit desperate... :-) ) In this particular sample we're analyzing muscle samples and ~700'000 lines of the total 4'000'000 lines belong to Titin (A2ASS6). Could this possibly interfere with the subplot summarization? - But again, manual removal of all Titin-related entries did not fix the memory overflow issue...
> > >
> > > Regarding the suggested MSstatsSummarize function: Is this equivalent to the dataProcess function? I will definitely look into this. Do you have an example workflow on how to implement this new function available?
> > >
> > > Thank you once more for all your help!
> > >
> > > Best regards,
> > > Christian
> > >
> > > mt...@mstaniak.pl schrieb am Dienstag, 22. März 2022 um 12:00:08 UTC+1:
> > > > Hi,
> > > >
> > > > this seems to be an R/Rstudio issue: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51248293/error-vector-memory-exhausted-limit-reached-r-3-5-0-macos

> > > > Mateusz

messages.body_plain:

phos.msstats <- SpectronauttoMSstatsPTMFormat(
  phos,
  fasta = "fgcz_9606_reviewed_cnl_20220429.fasta",
  Protein.data = prot,
  annotation = NULL,
  intensity = "PeakArea",
  filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
  qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
  useUniquePeptide = TRUE,

  removeNonUniqueProteins = TRUE,
  modificationLabel = "Phospho",
  removeiRT = TRUE,
  summaryforMultipleRows = max,
  which.Conditions = "all"
)

If someone could give me an idea where to start troubleshooting I would really appreciate it.

Cheers

A

messages.subject: MSstats 4.1.1 changes
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Love all the work that you all do for this package!

After the course at ASMS, I've been trying to learn how to use it and I've noticed that some output has changed. I've been following this tutorial https://msstats.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/MSstats_v3.18.1_manual_2020Feb26-v2.pdf. However, using the inbuilt data `DDARawData` gives me a different result from what's in the tutorial.
In particular, I'm referring to the output of `dataProcess()` which now only has Protein and Features level data. Attached here is the code that I ran. This is probably because of a new version of `MSstats`.

`DDA2009.proposed <- dataProcess(raw = DDARawData,
normalization = 'equalizeMedians',
summaryMethod = 'TMP',
censoredInt = "NA",
MBimpute = TRUE,
maxQuantileforCensored=0.999)
`

`names(DDA2009.proposed)`
`## [1] "FeatureLevelData" "ProteinLevelData" "SummaryMethod"`

Could you suggest how to run the differential expression results in this new situation? Or do you have a new tutorial that described the changes?

Thanks a lot,

Anna

messages.body_plain:

I really appreciate all the work the group puts into making standardized proteomics analysis packages. Until recently I was making functions in R to analyze proteomics data but eventually ran into some issues when I had to normalize between multiple kits. Thats when I decided to jump ship to MSstats. A little background on my data, its TMT labeled, with a phosphoenriched fraction and an input fraction. All files were searched together in PD2.5.

The issue I'm having is trouble creating the ProteinName + PTM site annotation column. The PD PSMs PTM output file isn't great. It contains a column of modifications that contain all PTMs, if a site isn't perfectly localized it appeart to just choose 1. The other PTM column is ptmRS site column which contains all site and there localization probability. My question is how should i make the PTM annotation column?
I've read in previous posts here that you're still working on a function to convert the PD PTM output into an MSstats class file and wanted to know how that coming and if i could test  that out?

Appreciate the help.
Best,
Scott
